body: Reopening to find less intrusive solution.

@trustin what about this idea:

For every remove and replace method in ChannelPipeline we add another one that takes a boolean parameter which tells if the remaining bytes or messages should be dropped or forwarded to the next handler in the pipeline.  This way we can either clear the buf or transfer it contents to the next in the pipeline on removal /replace. So we not need  to take any extra steps on removal in the handler itself as after the remove/replace call we are sure the actual buffer of the handler is empty. We could discard the content of the buf by default ( when a method without the boolean argument is used). This will also fix #858 and so give the user less surprises. 

I think I would go even futher and change all remove / replace methods to just  return the ChannelPipeline.

WDYT?
also one think to keep in mind is how to handle the forwarding of the elemnts if we have a bounded buffer and it can't take all of them. Maybe a throwing a special exception is good enough?

As I commented in the commit, I think we can just allow a user access the discarded data so that the user can forward it to the next buffer.  The question would be: how do we provide an access to the discarded data?  How about adding a `Buf` parameter to `ChannelPipeline.remove/replace()` so that the pipeline can flush the discarded data into the specified buffer?
This would work.. But I think we should also provide a shortcut for this with a boolean flag to just "forward" to the next handler.

Without shortcut:

```
pipeline.remove("name", ctx.nextOutboundByteBuffer());
```

I guess this seems short enough, no?
Maybe... Let just go with that and if we need something else we can process from here.. @trustin you want to "take it" or should I do later today ?
Please take this.  I'll review bounded buffer pull request.  :-)
